evidence: symmetry_check compared the ΔPDF's x–y section at one z (default 0; web/src/llm/tools/defs/symmetry_check.ts:35) with its images under the cell's in-plane operations only, chosen from the cell's metric and not from the operations the raw file declares (sectionSymmetry, web/src/llm/metrics/symmetry.ts:30-90; symmetry_check.ts:41): hexagonal, the six-, three- and two-fold and the a ↔ b mirror; orthogonal, the mirrors ⊥ a and ⊥ b, the two-fold, and the four-fold when a = b. An operation that moves c (a mirror ⊥ c, a two-fold ⊥ c, a cubic three-fold, the inversion) was never tested, so a ΔPDF could break one and pass: the symmetry's rule judges the operations it is given (web/src/llm/verdicts/rules.ts:469-478), and the ΔPDF's card reads that verdict (web/src/llm/verdicts/readers.ts:445, web/src/llm/report/report.ts:322). The transform keeps the data's even part (src/nebula3d/analysis/delta_pdf.py:326), so the ΔPDF is centrosymmetric and an operation and its product with the inversion are one test: on the x–y section through the origin the two-fold ∥ c held by the inversion alone, and a correlation off that plane broke the mirror ⊥ c unseen. On a constructed m-3m ΔPDF with a pair ±(0.35, 0, 0.4) (fractional) on the x–z section, the old check read every in-plane operation within 5.1e-8, while the mirror ⊥ c is off by 0.076 on the x–z and y–z sections. The check also judged lattice operations the declared group lacks (the mirrors ⊥ a and ⊥ b of data symmetrised with 4/m on a square cell, the four-fold of mmm), which no symmetrisation keeps. The ΔPDF evaluation's max_symmetry_break (web/src/llm/tune/evaluate.ts:87) tested the same in-plane operations whatever the file declared.
proposed_fix: Test each operation of the declared point group (symmetry_ops, closed into its group, acting on real space as its transpose), those that move c included, on the sections it maps onto sections: the x–y sections at z and −z, and the x–z and y–z sections through the origin, read through the client as before (four slices at most). An operation that maps none of them onto one is tested on the voxels it maps from one onto another; one that mixes axes whose grid steps differ (in the cell's fractional units, past 0.05 voxel at the grid's edge) is not tested, and not_tested says why. The ΔPDF is centrosymmetric by construction, so an operation and its product with the inversion are one entry ("two-fold ∥ c / mirror ⊥ c"), tested once; a voxel an operation leaves where it is, or sends to its own inverse, is left out, so each member alone gives the pair's number. Each entry reports rms_difference (its worst section's), pairs and tested_on, the sections it was compared on (no moves_c: with the pairs every entry holds a member that moves c, so it said nothing). With no operations declared, the cell's in-plane ones, as before. The limit stays 1e-3, and an operation that moves c is judged as one that keeps it. With no operation tested the verdict is not judged, and says why; with some untested and the rest holding it passes and says how many. The ΔPDF evaluation's max_symmetry_break tests the same group, those of its operations that map the x–y section through the origin onto itself (with none declared, as before).
